newsitem.title: USA: Boeing says market does not justify larger 747.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says market does not justify larger 747.

text.p: Boeing Co executives said on Monday that market conditions do not justify a proposed larger version of the jumbo 747, and the company plans instead to focus on new derivatives of its 767 and 777 twin-engine jets.

In a news release, Boeing commercial airplane group President Ron Woodard said the manufacturer was sharply scaling back a project that had been aimed at building a new jumbo jet capable of carrying 550 people.
Woodard said the plane-maker would leave some employees on the so-called 747-X programme to continue to study a possible larger version of the four-engine plane.
"This remains one of the priorities of our product development efforts," he said. "When the market develops for such an airplane, we will be ready."

But he said the company plans to put more resources in the near term on developing new versions of the smaller widebodies, the 767 and 777 to meet rising demand for "long-range, medium-sized airplanes."

Boeing had been considering the possibility of a new, larger airplane for about three years including a joint study with partners of its European rival Airbus Industrie that looked at a potential all new, superjumbo airplane.
But now Airbus is going ahead with plans for its own superjumbo, dubbed the A3XX, that would be bigger than the 747.
Boeing said it had about 1,000 people working on the 747-X programme, more than half of whom would be shifted into new 767 and 777 models.

For example the company recently has begun offering a 767-400ERX that would increase the capacity of the current 767-300 by 10 to 15 percent. And Boeing mentioned a possible version of the 777 that would have a range of 10,000 miles (16,000 km), more than any other commercial jet.
